fieldMarks: Two incomplete black or dark brown collars across a narrow neck; large head, sometimes bright yellow; long tail (CPW; MDC).
Turquoise to green or brown back with many small light spots and dark bands; to about 36 cm (14 in) (CPW; MDC).
Breeding males most colourful, with turquoise and yellow scales; throat dark-spotted or yellow to orange (CPW).
Breeding females have orange-red bars or spots on the sides of the body and neck; juveniles have wide dark bands or large dark spots (CPW).
Adult males lack dark pigment in the gular fold, and the mouth lining is usually black (NatureServe; CPW).
behavior: Diurnal; basks on boulders, hides under large rocks or in crevices when approached, and may run on its hind limbs (MDC).
Males defend territories; in Oklahoma about 6.4 dominant males per hectare (MDC; NatureServe).
Eats insects, spiders, other lizards and small snakes, occasionally plant material (MDC; NatureServe).
Active about March or April to October in the north; overwinters in burrows under large rocks (NatureServe; MDC).
habitat: Rocky areas with sparse vegetation: canyons, gullies, slopes, mesa tops and dry glades; often basks on boulders (CPW; MDC; NatureServe).
range: Southeastern Utah, southern Colorado, Kansas and central and southern Missouri south through Arizona, New Mexico, western and central Texas, Oklahoma and Arkansas into northern Mexico; Louisiana records may not be natural (NatureServe). Missouri populations north of the Missouri River appear introduced (MDC).

lookalikes.name: Great Basin collared lizard
lookalikes.howToTell: Great Basin lacks the black mouth lining and males have a compressed tail with a pale dorsal stripe (NatureServe).
